test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II (Statistics) Official Paper-II (Held On: 19 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: The mean and variance of a binomially distributed random variable X are 4 and 2, respectively. P(X = 2)is equal to:
solution:
**Given:**

Mean (μ) = 4

Variance (σ²) = 2

Binomial distribution: X ~ B(n, p)

Find P(X = 2).

**Concept:**

In a binomial distribution:

Mean, μ = n × p

Variance, σ² = n × p × (1 - p)

Probability formula: P(X = k) = ⁿCk × pk × (1 - p)ⁿ⁻k

**Formula Used:**

Mean: μ = n × p

Variance: σ² = n × p × (1 - p)

P(X = k) = ⁿCk × pk × (1 - p)ⁿ⁻k

**Calculation:**

Step 1: Solve for n and p using mean and variance.

⇒ μ = n × p = 4

⇒ σ² = n × p × (1 - p) = 2

Let p = probability of success.

⇒ n × p × (1 - p) = n × p - n × p²

⇒ Substitute μ = 4:

⇒ 4 × (1 - p) = 2

⇒ 4 - 4p = 2

⇒ 4p = 2

⇒ p = 0.5

⇒ Substitute p = 0.5 into μ = n × p:

⇒ 4 = n × 0.5

⇒ n = 8

Step 2: Solve P(X = 2).

⇒ P(X = k) = ⁿCk × pk × (1 - p)ⁿ⁻k

⇒ P(X = 2) = ⁸C² × 0.5² × (1 - 0.5)⁸⁻²

⇒ P(X = 2) = ⁸C² × 0.5² × 0.5⁶

⇒ ⁸C² = ⁸!/⁽²! × ⁽⁸⁻²⁾!⁾

⇒ ⁸C² = ⁸ × ⁷ / ² = 28

⇒ P(X = 2) = 28 × 0.5⁸

⇒ 0.5⁸ = 1/2⁸

⇒ P(X = 2) = 28 × 1/2⁸

⇒ P(X = 2) = 28/256

⇒ P(X = 2) = 7/64

⇒ P(X = 2) = 7/2⁶

**∴ P(X = 2) = ⁷/₂⁶, which matches Option 2.**
